overall.summary: Solid backend engineer with real production experience in Laravel and queue-based systems. GitHub activity backs up most CV claims, though the leadership claim is thin and testing depth is inconsistent across repos.

skills.name: Laravel / PHP backend development
skills.reasoning: Three of the candidate's four most-starred repos are Laravel applications using service classes, form requests, and queued jobs consistent with production-grade practice, not tutorial code.

skills.name: API design & integration
skills.reasoning: Repo `mkelsey/invoice-sync` implements a versioned REST API with resource transformers and rate-limit handling, matching the CV's claim of building a billing integration.

skills.name: Testing & code quality
skills.reasoning: Test coverage is present but shallow: two of three inspected repos have PHPUnit suites under 30% file coverage, and none use mutation testing or CI-enforced coverage gates.

claims.claim: Built and maintained a Laravel-based billing platform processing recurring invoices
claims.evidence: class InvoiceSyncService implements handles Stripe webhook reconciliation with idempotency keys and queued retry backoff
Senior Backend Engineer, Nov 2020 - Present; PHP Developer, Jun 2019 - Oct 2020

claims.claim: Wrote comprehensive automated test suites for every project
claims.evidence: tests/Feature contains 4 files covering 2 of 11 controllers

claims.claim: Led a team of 3 backend developers on the payments migration
claims.evidence: No commit co-authorship, PR review activity, or organization membership indicating a leadership role was found on the candidate's public GitHub profile

interview_questions.question: Walk me through how InvoiceSyncService handles a duplicate Stripe webhook delivery. What would break if the idempotency key check were removed?
ideal_answer_points: Explains idempotency keys prevent double-processing of retried webhook deliveries
Identifies that removing the check would cause duplicate invoice charges
Mentions the queued retry backoff as the source of duplicate deliveries

interview_questions.question: Only 2 of 11 controllers in invoice-sync have feature tests. How would you have prioritized test coverage on that project, and why weren't the others covered?
ideal_answer_points: Acknowledges the coverage gap honestly rather than deflecting
Proposes a risk-based prioritization (payment paths first)
Gives a credible reason for the gap (deadline pressure, legacy code, etc.)

interview_questions.question: Your CV mentions leading a team of 3 on the payments migration, but that isn't visible in your public repo activity. Describe your actual role and responsibilities on that migration.
ideal_answer_points: Gives specific, concrete examples of decisions or reviews they drove
Clarifies whether 'led' meant technical lead vs. people management
Names teammates or artifacts (PRs, design docs) that corroborate the claim

criteria.name: Laravel / PHP backend development
criteria.description: Depth and recency of production PHP/Laravel work, not tutorial or bootcamp projects.

criteria.name: API design & integration
criteria.description: Ability to design, version, and secure REST APIs and third-party integrations.

criteria.name: Testing & code quality
criteria.description: Presence and depth of automated tests, and general code hygiene.

rubric.scale: 0-100, weighted average rounded to nearest integer

fairness_note: No protected attributes (age, gender, ethnicity, nationality, religion) were used in this assessment.
